title: Germany – Pumps – Los 2.4 Lieferung Pumpen Wärmespeicher
description: Im Rahmen des Projekts „Errichtung Großwärmespeicher und dessen hydraulische Einbindung in die Fernwärmeverteilung am Standort HKW West“ (Gesamtprojekt WSPW) der Stadtwerke Karlsruhe soll ein Wärmespeicher zur Sicherstellung einer nachhaltigen, zukunftsfähigen und gesicherten Wärmeversorgung realisiert werden. Die verfahrenstechnische Aufgabe des zu planenden 2-Zonen-Wärmespeichers soll in der Speicherung und bedarfsgerechten Bereitstellung thermischer Energie innerhalb des Fernwärmesystems bestehen. Der drucklos ausgeführte Wärmespeicher soll durch die Ausbildung einer thermischen Schichtung die getrennte Aufnahme und Abgabe von Wärme auf unterschiedlichen Temperaturniveaus ermöglichen. Durch die hydraulisch entkoppelte Einbindung in das Fernwärmenetz über ein separates Vor- und Rücklaufsystem soll der Wärmespeicher zum Ausgleich von Lastschwankungen sowie zur zeitlichen Entkopplung von Wärmeerzeugung und -verbrauch beitragen. Bei diesem Beschaffungsvorhaben sollen funktionstüchtige Vor- und Rücklauf- sowie Beimischpumpen einschließlich aller zum bestimmungsgemäßen Betrieb erforderlichen Komponenten innerhalb der spezifizierten Liefergrenzen geplant, hergestellt und geliefert werden.

title: Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

title: Q--MOJAVE TORTOISE BIOINFORMATICS
description: PRESOLICITATION NOTICE The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) intends to issue a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a sequencing facility to conduct de novo epigenetic methylation clock development for the Mojave Desert tortoise using whole-genome enzymatic methylation and 5-base workflow, including the preparation and sequencing of DNA samples for methylation analysis, delivery of sequencing data, and de novo epigenetic methylation clock development. The objective is to generate data and identify loci that will be used to age tortoises. The Government anticipates awarding a firm-fixed-price purchase order for these services. Service Contract Act (SCA) is applicable and the wage determination corresponding to the location of performance will apply. ACQUISITION PROCEDURES This acquisition will be conducted using the simplified procedures for commercial products and commercial services under RFO Part 12. In accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2), for acquisitions at or below the Simplified Acquisition Threshold, the Contracting Officer may solicit quotations directly from suppliers. When using direct solicitation procedures, the Government will: 1. Post a presolicitation notice in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) in accordance with RFO Subpart 5.1, unless an exception applies; 2. Solicit quotations from at least three sources; and 3. Whenever practicable, solicit quotations from two sources not included in the previous solicitation. Accordingly, the Government intends to solicit quotations directly from a minimum of three qualified sources. In accordance with RFO 5.201(b)(2), this presolicitation notice is being posted to the GPE in lieu of posting the solicitation itself to the GPE. The RFQ will be provided directly to the sources selected for solicitation. INTERESTED SOURCES Interested, responsible sources that wish to be considered for this requirement may submit the following information: - Company name; - Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); - Business size and socioeconomic status; - Point of contact, telephone number, and email address; and - A brief statement demonstrating the firm's capability to perform the required services briefly described above. Interested firms should submit this information to Contracting Office Joahnne Ongjoco by email at Joahnne_Ongjoco@ios.doi.gov no later than the response date and time listed above. The Government may use responses to this notice to identify additional qualified sources for direct solicitation. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ). This presolicitation notice is for informational and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will issue the RFQ directly to selected sources in accordance with RFO 12.201-1(c)(2). All responsible sources responding to this notice will be considered by the Government in determining the sources to be solicited.

title: 6835--BULK OXYGEN - Bridge
description: This Special Notice of Intent (NOI) is not a request for competitive proposals.� This is not a solicitation or request for offers. � The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Loma Linda Healthcare System (LLHCS), intends to award a delivery order on a sole source basis to the incumbent RCG of North Carolina, LLC for the provision of bulk medical oxygen, including delivery, rental of the main storage tank, and rental of the backup tank. The previous contract option period was not exercised within the required timeframe, resulting in the facility relying on short term, month to month purchase orders to prevent disruption of service. Bulk medical oxygen is mission critical for patient care, life sustaining equipment, and overall hospital operations. Any lapse in supply would pose unacceptable risks to patient safety. This bridge acquisition is required to maintain uninterrupted oxygen delivery while the Department completes the necessary acquisition documentation and conducts competitive procurement for a long term follow on contract. This action is being taken pursuant to FAR 13.106 1(b), which permits sole source awards when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 325120. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6835. Any response to this notice must show clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. � A decision by the Government not to conduct competitive procurement for the proposed order based upon response to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All inquiries shall be submitted via email to Anthony.delacruz@va.gov.

title: H365--460-27-1-132-0001 | SPE 49273 | VISN 4 Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) | NCO 4 Services 3 (VA-27-00003148)
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12 of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This Solicitation is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ), and the solicitation number is 36C24426Q0969. This notice incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 effective 13 March 2026, and the Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulations (VAAR). The complete text of any of the clauses and provisions may be accessed in full text at FAR | Acquisition.GOV. This acquisition is� set aside for Service Disable Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB)concerns. The Government reserves the right to make a single award, multiple awards, no awards as a result of this solicitation. The Government may determine that it is in its best interest to make awards to more than one quoter. The NAICS code is 541380 Testing Laboratories and Services and the Product Service Code (PSC) is H365 Inspection Medical, Dental, and Veterinary Equipment and Supplies. The business size standard is $19 Million. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at� www.acquisition.gov. Solicitation number 36C24426Q0969 is issued with the possibility of an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for� Radiation Safety Officer and Physicist duties at Pittsburgh, Erie, Butler, Coatesville, Wilkes Barre, Altoona, Wilmington, Philadelphia, and Lebanon VA Medical Centers. Typical task orders under this contract will range from $1,500.00 to $250,000.00 with a maximum task order limit of $350,000.00. The duration of this MATOC shall be five (5) years, unless the $6,000,000.00 ceiling is met before. If a contractor is not awarded a task order of at least $1,500.00 during the terms of the contract, the contractor will be paid the guaranteed minimum amount of $1,500.00, at the end of the contract. The Seed Service Task Order may be awarded to one contractor who is awarded one of the MATOC contracts: Project 460-27-1-132-0001, Wilmington Radiation Safety Officer/Physicists Services. Complete instructions for submitting a response to this solicitation and applicable provisions and clauses are found in 36C24426Q0969. All quoters are advised to pay careful attention to the quote submission instructions as there are very specific instructions as what is required to be provided. Quoters will be evaluated based on their quoted response to the seed task order for radiation safety officer and radiation physicist services at the Wilmington VAMC. This seed project serves as a representative sample task and will be used to assess each quoter's technical capability, staffing approach, and understanding of the requirements applicable to the overall MATOC scope. Award of the MATOC will be based on this evaluation, with the seed project not guaranteed as an awarded task order. The period of performance (POP) is estimated to be 11/15/2026 11/14/2031. Should issuance of the IDIQ occur on a different date, the performance period will be adjusted accordingly. Any award resulting from this solicitation will be issued on a Standard Form 1449. NOTE: To receive an award resulting from this solicitation, offerors MUST be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database. Registration may be done online at: www.acquisition.gov or www.sam.gov. Any questions or concerns regarding this solicitation should be forwarded in writing via e-mail to the contract specialist, Matthew Wright at matthew.wright6@va.gov. No questions will be answered after 21 October 2026, 10:00 AM EST. Point of Contact Matthew Wright Contract Specialist Services 3 (Medical Equipment Maintenance Services) Department of Veterans Affairs/Network Contracting Office 4 Matthew.wright6@va.go

title: Medicaid Data Analysis for Bacterial Respiratory Pathogens and Information Systems
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded a sole source contract with MATHEMATICA INC., 1100 1ST ST NE FL 12, WASHINGTON, DC. 20002 This notice is provided in accordance with RFO FAR 8.401 & GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) . Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, Division of Bacterial Diseases (DBD) requires support Services with the contractor listed above. The requested contractor Mathematica qualified as �innovator status� vendor for data analysis by Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Mathematica also has demonstrated experience and specialized staff with unique access and analytical capabilities for Medicaid data sets which captures the largest segment of US healthcare data, including births. The contractor shall perform analyses across four technical dimensions defined in the Statement of Work: (1) validating infant GBS case counts using TAF OT claims and evaluating a fourth case definition tied to maternal Medicaid IDs; (2) developing and refining a probabilistic mother-infant linkage algorithm using the Medicaid Case Number and supplementary variables; (3) estimating maternal vaccination coverage (COVID-19, influenza, Tdap, and prospectively RSV) accounting for bundled payment code effects; and (4) applying methods to reduce gestational age missingness using prenatal claims data. These tasks require continuity with linkage algorithms and case-definition logic Mathematica has already built and validated under prior CDC task orders. The authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title III of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (41 U.S.C. 251, et seq.); Title 40 U.S.C. 501, Services for Executive Agencies, as implemented at FAR 8.401 and GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) "Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions are unique or highly specialized." Through its prior contracts, Mathematica has already built key parts of this analysis�including updating the medical codes used to identify cases, working to link mother and infant records more completely, and adjusting for how individual states handle Medicaid enrollment for newborns. This steady, hands-on progress means Mathematica starts this next phase of work already ahead, with the knowledge and tools in place that a new contractor would not have. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation to Robin C. Meyer, Contract Specialist, at rcm2@cdc.gov, which shall be considered by the agency. The deadline for submissions is Ocotber 31, 2026 at 4:30PM EST. The Government will review any/all information submitted to determine if other responsible sources exist that could provide this requirement. Information received in response to this announcement will be used solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

The US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, is conducting market research to identify potential parties having interest in and capability of performing construction of a new, fully functional, industrial, compressed air plant in the controlled access B18 Complex at Wright-Patterson AFB, including two centrifugal air compressors (4,000 HP), two industrial, natural gas-fired air heaters (18.1 MM BTU/hr / 55 MM BTU/hr), insulated specialty steel distribution piping (schedule 80-120), valves, and all associated controls and monitoring devices, integrated with the existing control system. Based on the responses to this request via the Market Survey Response Form, this requirement may be set-aside for small business (in full or in part) or procured through full and open competition. All Small Business Set-Aside categories will be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluation will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. The Government will consider feedback received in determining if a small business set-aside is appropriate for this requirement. DISCLAIMER: This request for information is for information purposes only; it is not a request for competitive proposals, quotations, or bids. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No Funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents to the announcement is strictly voluntary and will not be returned to the responder. Incomplete answers in any section or providing information outside the scope of this announcement may remove respondents from the Government's determination of whether to solicit the referenced project on a set-aside basis in accordance with Part 19 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future request for competitive proposals, quotations, or bids, if any issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement.

description: The USDA Forest Service (FS), Procurement & Property Services (PPS) is issuing this special notice as a means of complying with Contracting Desk Book, SUBPART 413.3 - Simplified Acquisition Methods, 413.303 Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs). The USDA FS intends on awarding a competitive BPA Call Order against the LMIR BPA for Western Divide Resiliency and Restoration Project Environmental Analysis of approximately 16,556 acres of National Forest System lands managed by the Eastern Divide Ranger District of the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests 12363N23Q4023 The Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) is a National BPA that consists of a large variety of work including Professional Services, Natural Resources Restoration, Project Management, NEPA, Communications, and more. The BPA can be utilized on all Forests and Grasslands and is available for all federal agencies to utilize. This is not a solicitation. This synopsis notification of intent to award a BPA Call order does not constitute a request for proposals or submission of any information in response to this notification. This procurement is restricted to those approved companies eligible for call orders under the Land Management Integrated Resources BPA (LMIR) for USFS. There are currently 58 businesses that will receive this solicitation. The Call Order shall be issued via email to those companies listed on the BPA. Any changes to the Call Order RFQ shall also be emailed to those companies listed on the BPA. Point of Contact is sm.fs.lmirbpa@usda.gov. This requirement will be competitively awarded as a BPA Call Order against the multiple award schedule BPA continuously solicited on the GPE at: SAM.gov. If contractors are not on the LMIR BPA and wish to join, they can respond to the BPA during the onboarding window which is Oct 1-Oct 31st each year for the life of the BPA. For instructions on how to join the BPA, search �Contract Opportunities� on sam.gov using solicitation number �12363N23Q4023� or emailing the LMIR BPA team for a list of onboarding instructions.

title: Architect & Engineering Services, Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award (A&E) Contracts needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs required by Federal Prison Industries (FPI)
description: The Federal Prison Industries (FPI) intends to solicit and award a competitively negotiated Architect and Engineer (A&E) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Contract needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs. The Architect and Engineer (A&E) shall furnish professional architectural, engineering, and related technical services, as specified herein, to the United States Government, Department of Justice, Federal Prison Industries (FPI). The resulting contracts will consist of a one?year base period and will include options for four additional one?year periods. All work performed under this contract shall pertain to projects located at FPI facilities within the contiguous United States. Pursuant to the terms of this contract, the A&E may be required to perform services under the following major categories, including other closely related services as necessary: � Review design and construction documents prepared by other A&E firms or by FPI personnel. � Prepare, develop, and produce design and construction documents for new facility construction, facility additions, and renovation or modernization of existing facilities. � Develop detailed and accurate cost estimates for construction activities, renovations, contract modifications, and claims. � Conduct Value Engineering (V/E) analyses and perform additional cost evaluation studies, as required. � Develop, maintain, and update project schedules and construction schedules. � Provide assistance in preventing, mitigating, and resolving disputes or claims arising from design or construction activities. � Furnish comprehensive architectural and engineering services encompassing all disciplines necessary to ensure the successful execution and completion of assigned projects. � Provide, as required, studies; design development; construction documents; technical specifications; support during bid negotiation; construction administration; and project closeout services. � Develop procedures, prepare construction documents and work statements, support master planning efforts, conduct regulatory compliance evaluations, and assist in the preparation of design?build documentation. � Prepare construction specifications that uphold the principles of full and open competition. � Comply with all general requirements applicable to task orders issued under this contract. In accordance with the Brooks Architect-Engineer Act, award(s) shall be made to the successful firm(s) based on demonstrated competence and qualifications to perform the services at fair and reasonable prices. Prior to this solicitation issuance, technical evaluations were conducted. This solicitation was then issued to the most highly rated firm(s). Therefore, in response to the solicitation, consideration for a contract award will be based solely upon the hourly rates, overhead and profit that are proposed and found to be fair and reasonable. Offerors are advised that award maybe made without discussions. Therefore, the initial proposal should provide sufficient information to recommend award without discussions and should reflect the offeror�s ability to perform at a reasonable price.

title: Leather Sheepskin Hair Type
description: Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support (DLATS), Clothing & Textiles (C&T) Directorate, is conducting research to determine industry capabilities for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This is a Sources Sought only and not a solicitation for proposals. This announcement is considered Market Research in accordance with FAR 10. DLA is the Defense Department�s principal buyer of multiple items within the Clothing & Textile industry that uses Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. Numerous item specifications utilize Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type as a component in a wide variety of items purchased by DLA Troop Support, such as AR/PD 12-01 with Change 8 Amendment 1 and AR/PD 17-06 with Amendment 3, for Helmet Retention Systems. The primary purpose of this announcement is to identify potential sources with domestic manufacturing capabilities of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This announcement also seeks to determine the availability of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type production capacity, limitations and challenges. Domestic sources using Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type with domestic manufacturing capabilities are required in accordance with DFARS 252.225-7002-2(c) Preference for Certain Domestic Commodities (DEC 2017) All potential sources will be U.S. based. Additional market research may be conducted prior to posting any solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this Sources Sought, nor will the Government compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing the information provided to the Government. This Source Sought does not constitute a commitment from the Government and any information provided in response to this Sources Sought will be used for informational purposes only. Any proprietary information submitted will be protected if appropriately marked. Vendor participation is not a promise for future business with the Government. The information for the below items is provided for informational purposes. It is highly recommended that vendors review the technical documents for items you can support then decide to request specifications. Vendors should use the following link to request item Specification: https://www.dla.mil/TroopSupport/ClothingandTextiles/SpecRequest.aspx Please use the contract opportunity notice ID �Sources Sought Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type� to obtain access. Fill in the request for the Technical Package requirements needed and under Special Instructions annotate �URGENT � MARKET RESEARCH � EXPEDITE.� The applicable North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) is 315990 Apparel Accessories and Other Apparel Manufacturing. Small business size standards matched to industry NAICS codes are published by the Small Business Administration and are available at http://www.sba.gov/content/table-small-business-size-standards. Contractors must be registered with the Central Contractor Registration (CCR) at System for Award Management (SAM) http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for an award. Representations and certifications must also be on record. Submission requirements: Responses to this Sources Sought must be sent to Ryan Reynolds Contract Specialist, via email at Ryan.Reynolds@dla.mil and to Michelle Falkowski, Contracting Officer, via email at Michelle.Falkowski@dla.mil by the response date in this notice and should include company name, CAGE code, company size/profile, any other supportive information and answers to the below questions for each item for which you are potentially interested in supplying/supporting. 1. What is the absolute minimum quantity required for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 2. What is your monthly minimum and maximum production capacity? 3. What is your current and maximum production rate of yards per week? 4. What is the minimum monthly production quantity required to be economically producible? 5. What is your available operating capacity at present? 6. What is the availability of the local labor pool? 7. Provide your Production Lead Time (PLT) for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. 8. Are there any issues with the availability of raw materials? 9. Please provide a summary of your current supply situation in terms of raw materials including major components, critical materials, lead-time issues, and suppliers. 10. Are you a supplier, distributor, contractor, or other of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 11. What is the country of origin of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type from your company? 12. In what country is your CAGE/NCAGE associated? Any information provided is voluntary.

title: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille
description: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille Hankinnan kohteena on Suomen Reumaliitto ry:n järjestämien Arkea tukevien -kurssien majoitus-, ruokailu- ja ryhmätilapalvelut. Hankinta koskee vuosina 2027 ja 2028 järjestettäviä kursseja. Lisäksi on mahdollisuus kahteen (2) optiovuoteen. Tarjouksia pyydetään kuudelta alueelta: Keski-Suomi, Pirkanmaa, Pohjois-Pohjanmaa, Pohjois-Savo, Päijät-Häme ja Helsinki-Uusimaa. Kursseja järjestetään vuosittain kahdeksan (8) valtakunnallisesti eri paikkakunnilla tilaajan määrittämällä tavalla. Kurssit ovat kestoltaan kahdesta vuorokaudesta (perjantaista - sunnuntaihin) neljään vuorokauteen (maanantaista -perjantaihin). Kursseilla on 16 -18 henkilöä. Kurssit on tarkoitettu aikuisille henkilöille, joilla on reuma tai muu tuki- ja liikuntaelinsairaus. Kurssipaikan majoitus-, ryhmä- ja ravintolatilojen tulee olla esteettömiä, jotta liikuntarajoitteiset henkilöt pystyvät toimimaan niissä. Invahuoneita tulee olla kahdesta kolmeen (2–3) kappaletta. Kurssipaikalle tulee voida saapua ja poistua julkisilla yhteyksillä, joiden pysäkki tai asema on enintään 500 metrin päässä kurssipaikasta (tai tarjoajan on mahdollista järjestää kuljetus kauempana olevalta pysäkiltä tai asemalta). Kaksi kursseista on luontopainotteisia, joten pihapiiristä tai lähiympäristöstä tulee löytyä helposti saavutettavia ja esteettömiä luontoreittejä. Kurssit järjestetään Sosiaali- ja terveysjärjestöjen avustuskeskuksen (STEA) myöntämällä valtionavustuksella. Hankittavan palvelun laajuus ja määrä perustuvat tulevan valtionavustuksen suuruuteen. Vuodelle 2027 myönnettävä valtionavustuksen määrä vahvistuu alkuvuodesta 2027. Hankinnan kohde ja sitä koskevat vaatimukset kuvataan tarkemmin liitteissä.,

The Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6 intends to release a solicitation for construction services for project 652-24-101 Improve Electrical Distribution at the Central VA Health Care system in Richmond, VA. title: Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy:n teollisuushalli Raonhaka 1
description: Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy:n teollisuushalli Raonhaka 1 Kannuksen Teollisuuskylä Oy on Kannuksen kaupungin ja kehitysyhtiö YritysKannuksen omistama kiinteistökehitysyhtiö, jonka toiminnan tavoitteena on mahdollistaa kohtuuhintaisia teollisia kasvutiloja yrityksille Kannuksessa. Yhtiö hakee nyt seuraavalle hallihankkeelle edullista ja laadukasta hallivalmistajaa, joka toimii samalla hankkeen pääurakoijana. Pääurakoijan vastuulle kuuluu myös kohteen rakennesuunnittelu. Hankkeen tekniset ratkaisut pyritään tekemään siten, että lopputuloksena valmistuu laadukasta, mutta mahdollisimman kustannustehokasta toimintatilaa vuokralaisena toimiville teollisuusyrityksille. Pääsuunnittelun on toteuttanut Arkkitehtitoimisto Paloranta Oy, LVISA-suunnittelusta vastaa Ratech Oy. Kannuksen Raonhaan teollisuusalueelle suunniteltu noin 1000 m2 teollisuushalli toteutetaan kahdessa osassa. Tässä tarjouspyynnössä pyydetään tarjoamaan nyt rakennettavan neljän lohkon kokonaisuuden kokonaishinta, sekä mahdollisten lisätöiden tuntihinta. Ensimmäiset neljä lohkoa rakennetaan piirustusten mukaisesti ensin, loput kaksi lohkoa laajennetaan heti, kun rakennettavat tilat on saatu täytettyä vuokralaisilla. Rakentaminen on tarkoitus aloittaa välittömästi, pohjatyöt pyritään saamaan valmiiksi ennen talvea, hallin pystytys ja varustelu talven aikana, käyttöönotto mahdollisimman nopeasti keväällä 2027. Laajennuksen rakentamisen aikataulua ei ole määritelty, mutta rakentaminen pyritään toteuttamaan saman pääurakoitsijan kanssa. Laajennuksen toteutuksessa käytetään tämän tarjouskilpailun hintaa, joka sidotaan kuitenkin laajennuksen osalta yleiseen kustannusindeksiin. Laajennuksen toteutuksesta laaditaan tulevaisuudessa oma sopimus ja aikataulu. Hankkeen käytännön toteutus on kuvattu Urakkaohjelmassa. Salassapito ja muut hankintaa koskevat seikat YSE 1998 mukaisesti. Tarjouksen vähimmäisvaatimukset, hylkäämisperusteet ja pisteytys on kuvattu omassa dokumentissaan.,

title: Industry Day: A Government-Industry Exchange on Construction Contracting - An Invitation for Industry Partners to Collaborate with the United States Space Force Operational Contracting Enterprise
description: Industry teammates, the Senior Contracting Official (SCO) for Operational and Enterprise Space Contracting invites you to a pivotal event discussing the future of construction in the U.S. Space Force. We are creating a forum to hear industry concerns and clarify the purpose of these new authorities to move faster, not to limit competition or replace valuable tools like Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACCs). description: The Permanent Secretariat of the Transport Community aims to conclude a service contract for preparation of the Study whose primary aim is to review the transposition of the TEN-T Regulation 1679/2024 in the Western Balkans region and to assess the current availability, quality, and compliance with the relevant EU legislation regarding the rest areas (RAs) and safe and secure parking areas (SSTPAs) along the Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) in the Western Balkans. The Study will deliver an inventory of RAs and SSTPAs along the TEN-T network (including border crossing points) in the Western Balkans populating TODIS (Transport Observatory Database/Information System) with these data, assessing their compliance with EU safety, security, and service standards. It will identify critical gaps, evaluate future demand, and provide policy, technical and investment recommendations for infrastructure upgrades. Furthermore, it will outline key findings and an action plan for implementation, supporting alignment with TEN-T requirements and enhancing road transport efficiency and safety. This Study could be helpful in situation that some of Western Balkans Regional Partners do not have defined locations and reserved spaces for RAs and SSTPAs within their spatial planning documentation. This Study will also enhance regulatory alignment with EU policies and practices. Specific tasks, deliverables, and requirements will be detailed and described in the Tender Specifications.

description: Del 1: Uppdraget avser busstransporter med busstorlek högst 22 passagerare och busstorlek över 22 passagerare och högst 55 passagerare. För elever i grundskolan är det i första hand badskjutsar tur och retur från skola till badhus (Navet) som efterfrågas. Badskjutsar är schemalagda, nya scheman skickas ut innan varje terminsstart. Resor föranledda av skolornas aktiviteter t.ex. resor till utbildning i andra skolor inom Umeå kommun, utflykter, skolresor och vid evakueringar när det sker ombyggnader av skolor. Vid badskjutsar ska avlämning ske 10 minuter före badtid, hämtning ska ske 20 minuter efter badtid om inte annan överenskommelse görs mellan parterna. Schema bifogas Del1.1: Uppdraget består resor beställda av verksamheter inom kommunen och övriga medverkande i upphandlingen som t.ex. vid konferenser, informationsdagar eller liknande och det kan vara resor över dagen eller resor med övernattningar. Bussar som ska användas i uppdraget ska vara anpassade för uppdragets utförande och inte vara större fordon än resan kräver. Del 2: Uppdraget avser busstransporter med 1 buss max 55 passagerare. Normalt sett används en buss men vid undantagsfall kan flera bussar krävas samtidigt. Kulturskolan bokar resor för såväl kommunala som fristående skolor och förskolor för transporter till/från kulturevenemang. Med kulturevenemang menas teater- och dansföreställningar, museibesök, biblioteksaktiviteter, konserter etc. Kulturbussen skjutsar inte till idrottsevent, friluftsdagar, simhall eller andra skolaktiviteter. Kulturbussen skjutsar förskolegrupper och klasser enbart inom Umeå kommun och kommundelar, enbart under skoltid 08.30-15.30. Kulturbussen bokas minst 10 dagar innan resan ska genomföras. Planering görs av kulturskolan terminsvis.

title: SYSTEM DELTA 84 (SYD 84/MT) MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT MISSILE WARNING / MISSILE TRACKING EPOCH 3 and EPOCH 4, REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)
description: SPACE SYSTEMS COMMAND (SSC) System Delta 84 (SYD 84/MT) MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT MISSILE WARNING / MISSILE TRACKING EPOCH 3 and EPOCH 4 **UPDATE** 21 August 2026** The Government has made available via DoD SAFE transmissions the following documents to interested vendors (in good standing on SAM.GOV) who have contacted the Government POCs in this RFI: (CUI) MEO Epoch 3&4 Industry Day Briefing 07_22_2026 (CUI) Epoch 3&4 Market Research RFI CUI Industry Day Q&A Document 08_20_2026 (CUI) Instructions for the Release of Attachments to MEO Epoch 3&4 Market Research RFI 08_20_2026 Additionally, the Primary Point of Contact (Contracting Officer/Agreements Officer) has been updated, to Capt Kerry Kearschner, USAF. Email: kerry.kearschner@spaceforce.mil. The following companies were added to the list of entities/contractors supporting SSC/SYD 84 and its affiliated government organizations: The Tech7 Company and Galaxia If the respondent disagrees with the release of its RFI response to any of the aforementioned firms, the respondent must clearly state this restriction in the cover letter accompanying the RFI response. **END OF UPDATE** Description SSC requests industry feedback on a Resilient Missile Warning and Tracking (MWT) Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) layer Epochs 3 & 4 (E3&4) production feasibility that will support MWT Full Warfighting Capabilities (FWC). The government is seeking industry feedback to inform the MEO E3&4 acquisition strategy and technical approach. The MEO MWT architecture is being incrementally developed in capability-based deliveries called Epochs. Each Epoch is expected to include at least one competitive award and allows for insertion of new technology and innovative solutions in response to progressive or updated warfighter requirements to ultimately meet Overhead Persistent Infrared (OPIR) capability needs. This RFI requests industry feedback and approaches to support delivering a MEO MWT E3&4 capability. The government encourages capability providers to offer responses for individual or multiple elements of the system architecture: Epochs 3 & 4 Space Vehicles (E3&4 SVs) - delivery, integration, and operations MEO Ground - ground segment with facilities and sites to operate the entire MEO MWT constellation with respect to Command and Control (C2) Digital Engineering Integration in alignment with Government Digital Engineering vision Contract Type The government is intending to use only Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract type with an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement. Feedback on this approach is welcome. Small Business Consideration The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 - Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). The small business size standard is 1,000 employees. Participation from small and small disadvantaged businesses is encouraged. SSC's Small Business points of contact can be reached at smallbus@spaceforce.mil or by phone at (310) 653-1108. Small Business Opportunities The government would like to encourage small business participation in the performance of this effort and requests insight into how your company would incentivize Small Business participation. Provide an assessment of potential subcontracting opportunities. Do you have any recommendations to increase small business participation under this effort? title: SOFTWARE LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: CorrelateIQ - Correlation-Based System Intelligence
description: CorrelateIQ reveals hidden relationships among many data streams at once, catching hidden patterns, early warning signs and operating shifts that single-variable monitoring overlooks. Built on analysis techniques from high-energy physics, this software from Los Alamos National Laboratory turns existing sensor and process data into practical insight that helps organizations prevent failures, protect quality and reduce downtime. Because the method makes no assumptions about where the data comes from, it applies to a wide range of numeric data, from manufacturing sensors and equipment logs to financial records, market data and scientific measurements. Overview Factories, laboratories, infrastructure networks, financial and real-estate markets now produce huge volumes of linked data from sensors, equipment logs and transactions. Most analytics tools, however, judge each variable separately or depend on fixed thresholds that trigger an alert only after a single reading crosses a limit. These methods have trouble spotting effects that arise from subtle interactions among many variables, such as gradual equipment wear, a drifting manufacturing process or a market entering a new phase. As a result, organizations often miss the earliest warning signals, react to failures only after they happen and leave much of the value in their data untapped. Teams in every data-reach fields need a practical way of understanding how an entire system behaves as a whole, not merely how each part performs alone. Key Benefits Spots early warning signs before small problems become costly failures Uncovers the hidden factors that drive outcomes such as quality, risk or price Reveals relationships across many data sources that conventional tools miss Identifies which combinations of variables matter most Gets more value from data organizations already collect Works across industries and data types, from factory sensors to financial records Condenses complex, high-volume data into clear, compact indicators Complements existing monitoring, machine learning and digital twin systems Core Capabilities At its core, CorrelateIQ: Correlation-Based System Intelligence measures collective behavior. Users choose the variables or signals of interest, and the software calculates higher-order correlations that capture how those inputs change together rather than separately. The framework accepts mixed data types, including time-series records, sensor readings, transactional data and scientific measurements. It condenses them into compact representations of overall system behavior. Because the software reduces many interacting variables to a smaller set of meaningful indicators, complex environments become easier to read, compare and act upon. CorrelateIQ also goes beyond a single snapshot. It tracks how correlation patterns change over time, so users can see shifts in operating state, new anomalies and transitions from one regime to another. Its outputs can act as an analytics or feature-generation layer that feeds existing monitoring, control or machine learning systems. It can run in real-time monitoring pipelines or offline analytics platforms. Planned improvements include automated selection and ranking of the most useful correlations, adaptive correlation building and closer integration with predictive maintenance and digital twin workflows. Use Cases & Market Applications Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing (process monitoring, quality control) Industrial operations and energy (predictive maintenance, equipment health) Infrastructure (structural health monitoring, multisensor networks) Industrial software and digital twins (system modeling, feature generation) Finance and real estate (market shift detection, risk analysis) Scientific research (physics data analysis, complex systems studies) Healthcare, transportation and cybersecurity (anomaly detection, early warning) Supply chains and climate monitoring (leading indicators, change detection) LA-UR-26-29216 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. The government is seeking industry feedback to inform the MEO E3&4 acquisition strategy and technical approach. This RFI requests industry feedback and approaches to support delivering a MEO MWT E3&4 capability. The government encourages capability providers to offer responses for individual or multiple elements of the system architecture: Epochs 3 & 4 Space Vehicles (E3&4 SVs) - delivery, integration, and operations MEO Ground - ground segment with facilities and sites to operate the entire MEO MWT constellation with respect to Command and Control (C2) Digital Engineering Integration in alignment with Government Digital Engineering vision Contract Type The government is intending to use only Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract type with an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) agreement. title: Medical Coding & Auditing
description: The VA Greater Los Angeles Health Care System had an urgent requirement for medical coding and auditing services. The Contractor must assign current, appropriate International Classification of Diseases (ICD), Common Procedural Terminology (CPT), and Healthcare Common Procedural Coding System (HCPCS) codes based on health record documentation for outpatient, surgical, and inpatient care and services provided at all Veterans Affairs Los Angeles Healthcare System locations. Additionally, the Contractor must conduct coding audits of inpatient and outpatient encounters as requested by the medical facility. This was an urgent requirement to ensure the timely and accurate processing of healthcare documentation and billing to prevent disruptions to veteran care. A three-month contract was urgently required to ensure uninterrupted service delivery while allowing sufficient time for the proper procurement and competition of a new long-term contract. Cooper Thomas was the only vendor able to meet this requirement because they are the incumbent contractor with an already-approved FITARA. Engaging a new vendor would necessitate a separate FITARA approval and a full onboarding process, both of which would introduce significant delays and risk to mission continuity. Therefore, to maintain continuity and meet urgent operational needs, only Cooper Thomas can fulfill the requirement within the necessary timeframe.

title: Performance Measurement for the Medicare Advantage Program
description: This posting provides notice that the Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) for the Performance Measurement for the Medicare Advantage Program procurement is being posted pursuant to GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(3)(i), which requires the ordering activity to publish a notice and post the justification within 14 days after placing an order exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold that is supported by an LSJ. Section 1859(f)(5) of the Social Security Act (�the Act�) requires that organizations offering specialized Medicare Advantage (MA) plans for special needs individuals have in place an evidenced-based model of care (MOC) with appropriate networks of providers and specialists. In addition, Section 1859(f)(7) of the Act requires that a Medicare Advantage Organization (MAO) offering a specialized MA plan for special needs individuals (i.e., special needs plan, or SNP) be approved by the National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) based on standards established by the Secretary. This requirement is implemented at 42 CFR ��422.101(f) and 422.152(g) and requires MAOs offering SNPs to have NCQA review and approve the required MOC each SNP submits to CMS on a regular basis. The Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set (HEDIS�) is a widely used set of health plan performance measures employed by both private and public health care purchasers to promote accountability and to assess the quality of care provided by managed care organizations. NCQA owns the proprietary rights to HEDIS� and the system that collects HEDIS� data. It is the only organization authorized to add quality measurements to HEDIS� and to provide technical assistance to commercial and Medicare health plans and auditors in the use of these measurements. Section 1853(o)(6)(A) of the Act states that the Secretary may require reporting of data under section 1852(e) for, and apply under this subsection, quality measures at the plan level for specialized MA plans for special needs individuals instead of at the contract level. The purpose of this task order is to support CMS in the evaluation and approval of each SNP�s model of care (MOC). As noted above, Section 1859(f)(7) of the Act and 42 CFR ��422.4(a)(1)(iv), 422.101(f), and 422.152(g) require that each MAO offering a SNP must submit a MOC to be approved by NCQA. Please see the Attachments section of this notice for a complete copy of the approved LSJ. Note - This is NOT an active procurement opportunity but is instead a required posting of an approved LSJ subsequent to task order award.

title: U.S. Embassy Tashkent - Transportation services in support of senior High Level USG VIP Visit
description: JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY Department of State Contracting Activity Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Tashkent, Uzbekistan Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy Tashkent- TRANSPORTATION SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF SENIOR HIGH LEVEL USG VIP VISIT SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED Approval is requested to award on a sole-source basis a Purchase Order, Firm-Fixed-Price commercial transportation services contract to Uzviptrans for a U.S. Embassy Tashkent visit planned for October 2026. SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS [x] 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2; Unusual and Compelling Urgency; (Based on the available time and urgency of the requirement as detailed below) Security concerns prohibit sufficient advanced notification of VIP travel to allow for sufficient time to conduct full and open competition. The Department of State can only communicate with the staff at Posts abroad when authorization is given due to security concerns. They have an extremely short turnaround time when authorization has been granted for negotiations to commence and site selections to be finalized with both the local vendors and Posts before the actual Senior High Level USG VIP visit occurs. The estimated value for the entire period of performance is $25,000.00 SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.103. Proposed authority: FAR 6.103-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR'S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED UZVIPTRANSSERVICE LLC (UzVipTrans) is uniquely qualified to meet the Government's transportation requirements due to its ability to provide coordinated transportation services for business meetings, official events, and VIP movements in Uzbekistan. The company provides point-to-point, hourly/as-directed, corporate, and airport transfer services and maintains a diverse fleet that includes business and premium sedans, SUVs, minivans, minibuses, and larger group transportation vehicles. The nature of this requirement requires a transportation provider capable of supporting changing schedules, multiple destinations, individual VIP movements, and group transportation under centralized coordination. UzVipTrans has the combination of vehicle categories and chauffeured transportation services necessary to support these requirements and accommodate different passenger capacities and operational needs. Using a single transportation provider will also provide consistent dispatching and coordination and reduce the operational risks associated with dividing transportation requirements among multiple companies during the event. SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER FAR 5.201 APPLIES The proposed contract was synopsized on August 18, 2026. The following other service providers were reviewed but were not adequate because of the following: Asia Adventures - does not have enough vans. Radius Travel - does not have sufficient number of vans. SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated $25,000.00 cost to the Government for the supplies/services covered by this J&A is expected to be fair and reasonable. This determination is based on the fact that the rates for transportation services are within the applicable Samarkand rate and offers a flexible cancellation policy. By signing this justification, the Contracting Officer determines that the anticipated $25,000.00 cost to the Government is fair and reasonable. SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED The market research included RFI sent to transportation companies in Samarkand to check availability for the required October 2026 period. SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION The acquisition supports a time-specific U.S. Embassy Tashkent visit in Samarkand during October 2026 and requires coordinated transportation services. Many of the arrangements for transportation are often not confirmed until just before the actual visit. In addition to supporting a large delegation within a short time frame, last minute and frequent changes of itineraries for supporting personnel often result in significant changes in how Posts work with the vendors. With the exception of a few trips, contracts are not permitted to be signed until the Department of State (Post) has written confirmation from all supporting agencies, which enables collection of funds from said agencies in the event of cancellation. This results in an unusual and compelling urgency in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), FAR 6.302-2. These unique Senior High Level USG VIP travel requirements result in only a single or a very limited number of responsible sources with no other supplies or services capable of satisfying agency requirement in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 253 (c) (2), Far 6.302-2. SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN INTEREST IN THE ACQUISITION To date, no other sources have written to express an interest in this acquisition. SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED For future requirements, the U.S. Embassy Tashkent will continue to conduct advance market research and assess whether other transportation providers can meet the Government's transportation requirements. If market conditions change or additional capable sources become available, future acquisitions for similar services will be competed to the maximum extent practicable.

description: This is the U.S. Embassy Riga Pre-Solicitation Notice only. Contractors are required to read the requirements below. No responses are requested by this notice. The U.S. Embassy Riga issues this notice with the intent of giving an opportunity to all interested parties to appropriately prepare for the anticipated Request for quotes (RFQ). This is not a request for proposal; this is for pre-solicitation/informational purposes only. No award will be made based on responses received to this notice. The requirement is to furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to remove the existing exterior facade lighting fixtures and install new RGBW LED facade lighting fixtures at the U.S. Embassy Riga, Latvia. U.S. Embassy Riga is currently illuminated by iGuzzini Linealuce B752 facade light fixtures. The Department seeks to replace these fixtures with individually addressable RGBW LED fixtures. To ensure rapid installation, ongoing maintenance, and ready access to materials and skilled labor, it is necessary to procure locally. U.S.-based fabricators are not positioned to service installations in Latvia, and sourcing materials or technical support from the United States would result in unacceptable delays and increased costs. Local procurement will ensure the Embassy can complete the work within the required timeframe and minimize future operational disruptions.

title: DA10--DB Protect Software and Maintenance Bridge (VA-26-00089068)(New Work)
description: This requirement was for a firm-fixed price delivery order (DO) issued under National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solution for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V Government wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) contract NNG15SD20B with Cynergy Professional Systems LLC (Cynergy) to provide brand name TrustWave Holdings Inc. (TrustWave) DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. Cynergy is a Small Business Administration Certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) that is an authorized reseller for brand name TrustWave DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. TrustWave DbProtect licensing and support are proprietary and can only be procured directly from an authorized TrustWave provider. Because the database security environment relies on TrustWave s unique architecture, integrations, and maintenance protocols, any attempt to obtain licensing or support through an alternate source would result in delays, incompatibility risks, and unacceptable gaps in security coverage. Cynergy is the current provider and will ensure uninterrupted protection of mission critical systems. Without the required TrustWave DbProtect licensing, the VA would be unable to perform essential database vulnerability scans, leaving critical systems unmonitored. This inability to assess and identify security risks would place the VA s data and infrastructure under undue and unacceptable risk. No other brand name database vulnerability scanning platform is interoperable with VA s existing TrustWave DbProtect infrastructure, database structures, and software application programming interfaces due to the proprietary constraints of the TrustWave infrastructure currently implemented within VA. Specifically, due to the proprietary constraints within the software source code, any other Original Equipment Manufacturer s (OEM) solution would not be able to communicate with the VA s existing TrustWave software licenses to provide the necessary database scanning and database vulnerability data collection, as well as critical updates, patches, updates to TrustWave DbProtect's Shatter Knowledge database, and bug fixes needed to ensure the infrastructure continues to function as intended.

title: NCFI Expansion Furniture
description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Secret Service, Office of Procurement, awarded a GSA Multiple Award Schedule delivery order to Business Interiors, Inc. for furniture, design, freight, and installation supporting the National Computer Forensics Institute�s facility expansion in Hoover, Alabama. The award includes furnishings for administrative offices, classrooms, auditorium and lobby areas, food-service space, and conference rooms. Required items include workstations, desks, chairs, collaborative seating, classroom electrostatic-dissipating desks, booths, couches, and conference-room furniture. The delivery order was awarded on a limited-sources basis under FAR 8.4, Only One Source (except brand name). Business Interiors was the only source capable of providing the required furnishings and services at the required level of quality because it was already integrated with the City of Hoover�s concurrent NCFI facility-expansion project. Its project-specific furniture layouts, approved product configurations, infrastructure coordination, and installation sequencing were necessary to ensure compatibility with the facility�s architectural plans, fixed furniture, power and data connections, construction schedule, and installation activities. Use of another vendor would have required duplicative site surveys, design and engineering coordination, product matching, and separate delivery and installation planning, creating increased cost, schedule delay, and integration risk. The attached redacted justification provides the supporting rationale for this award.

description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is planning to issue a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Bicalutamide Tablets. Procurement details follow. title: U.S. Embassy Tashkent - S Visit/organization and technical support of event in Samarkand in October 2026
description: JUSTIFICATION FOR OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION SECTION 1: IDENTIFICATION OF THE AGENCY AND THE CONTRACTING ACTIVITY Department of State Contracting Activity Overseas Post U.S. Embassy Tashkent, Uzbekistan Requiring Activity U.S. Embassy Tashkent- S Visit/organization and technical support of event in Samarkand in October 2026 SECTION 2: NATURE AND/OR DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION BEING APPROVED Approval is requested to solicit and award a firm-fixed-price contract on a sole-source basis to GUP "lnterForum" (State Unitary Enterprise InterForum) for integrated event organization, technical and design support services for S Visit in Samarkand in October 2026. SECTION 3: DESCRIPTION OF SUPPLIES/SERVICES REQUIRED TO MEET THE AGENCY'S NEEDS The Government requires one venue and contractor to plan, coordinate, furnish, install, operate the event services during S Visit. The scope of work includes: Venue spaces in Congress Hall: Ballroom, Sun Hall, Sapphire, Ruby, Topaz, Lazurite, Amber, and one-quarter of Grand Hall; Service personnel, table setting, and furniture rental; Event lighting and sound equipment; 150 square meters of LED screens; high-speed internet; Congress Center photo-zone banners, including 5 x 3 m and 12.7 x 5 m installations; floral arrangements; Visual identity, print and wayfinding materials, slides and screen graphics, animation, 3D Global Acquisitions U.S. DEPARTMENT of STATE renderings, decoration designs and drawings, production oversight, and event coordination; and Simultaneous-interpretation equipment: 10 equipment units, 200 headsets, and IO booths, as specified in the estimate. Total value: UZS 3,487,503,140 including base estimated services ofUZS 2,830,765,535 a 10% InterForum service fee ofUZS 283,076,554 and 12% VAT ofUZS 373,661,051. SECTION 4: IDENTIFICATION OF THE STATUTORY AUTHORITY PERMITTING OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION This acquisition is conducted under the authority of 41 U.S.C. 3304, as implemented by FAR 6.103. Proposed authority: FAR 6.103-1 - Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. SECTION 5: DEMONSTRATION THAT THE PROPOSED CONTRACTOR'S UNIQUE QUALIFICATIONS OR THE NATURE OF THE ACQUISITION REQUIRES USE OF THE AUTHORITY CITED GUP "InterForum" is only one company who has a venue capable to provide specified conference rooms and halls for high level visits, including the installation and operation of equipment, required decor, and the delivery of required services for the event dates. SECTION 6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS WERE SOLICITED FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS IS PRACTICABLE, INCLUDING WHETHER A NOTICE WAS OR WILL BE PUBLICIZED AS REQUIRED BY FAR SUBPART 5.2 AND, IF NOT, WHICH EXCEPTION UNDER FAR 5.201 APPLIES The proposed contract was synopsized on August 18, 2026. The following other hotels were reviewed but were not adequate because of the following: Movenpick Samarkand - doesn't meet security requirements. Hilton Garden Inn - does not have sufficient event facilities for required services SECTION 7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED COST TO THE GOVERNMENT IS FAIR AND REASONABLE The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated UZS 3,487,503,140 cost to the Government for the supplies/services covered by this J&A is expected to be fair and reasonable. This determination is based on the fact that the venue rates, service and equipment quantities, rates for design and production are reasonable and competitive with comparable market rates. By signing this justification, the Contracting Officer determines that the anticipated UZS 3,487,503,140 cost to the Government is fair and reasonable. SECTION 8. DESCRIPTION OF THE MARKET RESEARCH CONDUCTED (SEE PART 10) AND THE RESULTS OR A STATEMENT OF THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED Market research included requests for information sent to hotels and event facilities in Samarkand, as well as audiovisual and interpretation providers, florists, and design firms. The research assessed their capabilities, including IT support, and their availability during the required period in October 2026. SECTION 9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION The acquisition supports a time-specific U.S. Embassy Tashkent visit and event in Samarkand during October 2026 and requires coordinated venue access, event design, installation and operation of AV and interpretation systems, internet, decoration, and on-site management during a time-specific event. SECTION 10. LISTING OF THE SOURCES, IF ANY, THAT EXPRESSED, IN WRITING, AN TEREST IN THE ACQUISITION To date, no other sources have written to express an interest in this acquisition. SECTION 11. STATEMENT OF THE ACTIONS, IF ANY, THE AGENCY MAY TAKE TO REMOVE OR OVERCOME ANY BARRIERS TO COMPETITION BEFORE ANY SUBSEQUENT ACQUISITION FOR THE SUPPLIES OR SERVICES REQUIRED For future requirements, the U.S. Embassy Tashkent will continue to conduct advance market research and assess whether other facilities can meet the Government's conference, security, location, capacity, design technical requirements. If market conditions change or additional capable sources become available, future acquisitions for similar services will be competed to the maximum extent practicable.

title: 5650--American Lake B81 Lab Roof
description: INTRODUCTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20 anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single, Firm-Fixed-Price Construction Contract for the Roof Replacement at American Lake Facilities Maintenance Service at 9600 Veterans Dr. SW Tacoma, WA 98493. DESCRIPTION: The small flat roof above the laboratory storage rooms in Building 81 has experienced persistent leaks for several years. Although multiple repairs have been attempted, including large applications of tar, the roof continues to fail. The existing torch?down roof will be replaced with a TPO roofing system to provide a long?term solution. The area includes six AC units that cool the laboratory below and must remain functional nearly year?round. ADMINISTRATIVE: The solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) conducted in accordance with FAR Parts 12, 19, and 36 and will be evaluated in accordance with the procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be advertised as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Set-Aside. Proposals received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable NAICS Code is 238160 with a size standard of $19 Million. The solicitation is expected to be issued in FY 2026. The period of performance is approximately 120-Calendar days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. The Magnitude of Construction is expected to be between $100,000 and $250,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers.
